highlights.title: Fake 10 Downing Street listing exposes 'unfit' Booking.com, says consumer group
highlights.summary: Booking.com said the "limited test" was "not a true reflection of the experience of millions of listings or reviews".
body: Consumer group Which? says it was able to create a fake listing for 10 Downing Street on travel giant Booking.com.

The UK watchdog said its researchers were able to book a bogus stay at the prime minister's address - as well as leave a fake review noting "hanging out" with resident mouser Larry the cat as a highlight.
It said despite clear signs it was fake, Booking.com did not remove the listing until two months after it was uploaded.
They said because Which?'s listing was not "live" on its site across the two months it was present, "some of our automatic fraud controls were not triggered to completely remove the closed listing".
points: Booking.com said the "limited test" was "not a true reflection of the experience of millions of listings or reviews".

highlights.title: Walter Torous named executive director of MIT Center for Real Estate
highlights.summary: The senior lecturer, already director of the degree program, will now oversee all aspects of the center’s activities and operations.
body: Walter Torous, senior lecturer in the MIT Department of Urban Studies and Planning (DUSP) and the MIT Sloan School of Management, and director of the Master of Science in Real Estate Development Program (MSRED), was recently named executive director of the MIT Center for Real Estate (CRE) — effective July 1, 2026.

In announcing Torous’ appointment, School of Architecture and Planning Dean Hashim Sarkis also said that Justin Steil, professor of law and urban planning, will represent CRE as faculty chair of the Academic Curriculum Council.

“Together, Walter and Justin will guide CRE’s academic and strategic direction as it continues to strengthen its role within our school and the Institute,” Sarkis said. “Their appointments reflect the center’s distinctive position at the intersection of finance, design, planning, technology, and public policy — and its long-standing commitment to understanding real estate not only as a market force, but also as a driver of urban transformation and social change.”

highlights.summary: Everton's move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has fallen through after a change of heart from the player - after the deal scuppered Chelsea's chances of signing Lamine Camara.
body: Balogun arrived on Merseyside at lunchtime to complete the £40m Deadline Day transfer, but doubts then started to emerge about the deal being completed during the afternoon as the medical threw up an issue.

As a result of this issue, Monaco then proceeded with a move to sell midfielder Camara. But in another twist, Everton renegotiated the terms of the deal for Balogun - which forced a dramatic move from Monaco.
With a full agreement to sell Camara to Chelsea in place, Monaco withdrew from the deal as the 11pm transfer deadline passed, which left the Blues furious.
Chelsea also had the chance to withdraw from the £125m move to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City, but chose not to out of good faith.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Soars to No. 1 on Netflix's Movie Chart
highlights.summary: After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally starting to feel real — and fans have been desperate for every scrap of information they can get. Recent leaks offered glimpses of the game ahead of its official reveal, while Rockstar's latest footage confirmed that GTA 6 is shaping up to be…
body: So when Rockstar brought its latest GTA 6 footage to Netflix, it knew people would watch. The company probably didn't expect over 31.1 million people to do so in just a few days.

Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look, the nearly 27-minute gameplay showcase that premiered on Netflix last week, hit No. 1 on the English film list in 87 of the 93 countries tracked globally, according to Netflix. That's a pretty remarkable result for what is, essentially, a very long video game trailer. The showcase has also been uploaded to YouTube, where it's now passed 17 million views.
The Netflix showcase finally gave everyone a lengthy look at the game following two shorter trailers — and there was plenty to unpack.

For starters, Vice City is only part of the story. Rockstar says the playable area in GTA 6 will be roughly three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2 's playable map. The showcase gave us a better sense of that scale, jumping between the city, beaches, rural areas, and a Florida-inspired wilderness packed with wildlife.

body: The company is doing some AI safety damage control ahead of Astra’s release.

In July, an unreleased OpenAI model broke out of its restricted environment, finagled its way into internet access, made it possible for AI agents to secretly conspire under the company’s nose using a secret message board, and hacked into the network of AI lab Hugging Face. The attack sparked weeks of discussion and controversy inside and outside the AI industry, and AI leaders treated it as a “warning shot” for the tech’s growing capabilities and the inadequacy of its safeguards.

body: Coffee simply tastes better at a cafe – and if you have found yourself using this sentiment to justify dropping $10 on a latte each morning, you are not alone.

It does not have to be this way. To help you upgrade your at-home coffee game, we interviewed baristas, tested 10 milk frothers, tried every model of the AeroPress coffee maker and conducted our own blind taste test pitting instant against drip.
Years ago, I was convinced that my at-home coffee setup would not be complete without dropping $1,000 on a fancy espresso machine.

highlights.title: Here's our first look—and drive—of the 2027 Range Rover Electric
highlights.summary: Jaguar Land Rover provided flights from Washington, DC, to London and accommodation so Ars could visit its factory and drive the Range Rover Electric. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. Jaguar Land Rover was one of the first automakers to announce a transition away from combustion engines.
body: Because the idea was to make the Range Rover Electric a Range Rover first and an EV second, it looks virtually identical to the other versions, albeit with a slightly more aerodynamic front grille and more aero-efficient wheels that together conspire to shave off a fraction of the vehicle’s drag coefficient. The lack of tailpipes at the back is probably the biggest giveaway that you’re looking at the electric one. There’s also a flat underbody, but hopefully you’ll never need to look at that.

The current Range Rover uses JLR’s MLA architecture, which was designed over a decade ago to be powertrain agnostic. The BEV actually only weighs 165 lbs (75 kg) more than the V8; getting rid of the front, center, and rear differentials plus all their driveshafts saves almost as much weight as the battery and drive units add back. The front and rear drive units are identical permanent-magnet synchronous motors with an output of 349 hp (260 kW); a front-induction motor was considered but dropped due to heat management concerns. Combined output is 542 hp (404 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm).

highlights.title: OpenAI Is About to Release Its First AI Model With ‘Critical’ Cyber Abilities
highlights.summary: The company will give select partners early access to its Astra AI model—so they have time to shore up their defenses.
body: OpenAI announced Tuesday that its forthcoming AI model, Astra, is its first to reach the company’s threshold for what it calls “critical” cyber capabilities. OpenAI says it plans to publicly release a version of Astra “soon,” but will make the model’s advanced cyber capabilities available only to select partners in its Daybreak Blue early-access program at launch.

In a briefing with reporters, OpenAI safety and security leaders said the company has concluded that Astra reaches the critical cybersecurity capabilities outlined in its preparedness framework, which sets thresholds and protocols for when its AI models pose new levels of risk. The company says an AI model has reached its critical cyber threshold when it can independently find and exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities in real-world software. OpenAI leaders said the company has followed its procedure for this situation, which is to halt further development until appropriate safeguards and security measures can be implemented.
points: The company will give select partners early access to its Astra AI model—so they have time to shore up their defenses.

body: Camara was set to join Chelsea for £47m and was to sign a six-year deal pending a medical.
Just after the 11pm transfer deadline passed, news emerged that Monaco reneged on the agreement they had with Chelsea, and they had informed the Blues of their decision in writing.

Monaco only wanted to sell one player, and once they thought they had a deal agreed to sell Balogun to Everton, they pulled out of the Camara-to-Chelsea deal despite a full written club-to-club agreement with the Blues.

highlights.title: Sony To Pay Out Nearly $8 Million In Class-Action Settlement Over Game Prices
highlights.summary: Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices. The settlement ( via IGN ) comes after Sony's motion to dismiss the lawsuit was denied, and settlement class members across a more-than-four-year period are potentially eligible…
body: The lawsuit, originally filed back in 2024, alleged that Sony established a monopoly over PlayStation Store prices by making publishers "cede control over the final price to Sony" and that Sony "eliminated the last vestiges of price competition when it stopped allowing outside retailers to sell digital download codes that could be redeemed on the PlayStation Store."

Sony is not agreeing to wrongdoing as part of the settlement, and will be avoiding a civil trial if the terms are agreed upon by the court. Once that happens, the claims against Sony will be dismissed "with prejudice," meaning another lawsuit on the subject cannot be filed.

You are potentially eligible for a payout if you purchased one of the affected games via the PlayStation Store between April 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023. Dozens of games are listed in the official court documents, including Nier: Automata, Resident Evil 4, The Last of Us Remastered, and Vita games like Uncharted: Golden Abyss and Killzone: Mercenary.

highlights.summary: Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month. Financial terms have not been disclosed.
body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.

highlights.title: Guerlain 101: From Rouge G to Abeille Royale, the Products That Define the French Beauty House
highlights.summary: Nearly 200 years old, Guerlain remains relevant by being obsessed with innovation. Discover Vogue's edit of the best Guerlain products, from cult-favorite lipsticks to honey-powered skincare.
body: Guerlain has been a fixture of French luxury beauty for nearly 200 years. In an industry where new brands seem to appear overnight, maintaining that kind of longevity, and staying relevant throughout, is no small feat. As you can imagine, this has meant a lot of product launches; but according to the brand not every new idea is rushed to market.

“We take our time at Guerlain, waiting until we have something truly meaningful to offer the world,” CEO Gabrielle Saint-Genis tells Vogue. “When you’re a house that has been passionate about fragrance and cosmetics for 200 years, you are obsessed with innovating.”

One area this innovation has played out is Guerlain’s work with honey. For more than 15 years, Guerlain has developed a multi-parameter selection process to identify honeys with increasingly powerful repair activities, per Dr. Frédéric Bonté, Guerlain’s director of scientific communication. The research is far more involved than simply identifying different varieties of honey: It includes studying honeybees, analyzing the composition of the honey they produce, and examining the environments in which they live.

highlights.title: The Range Rover Electric: Specs, Price, Availability
highlights.summary: After long delays, JLR’s biggest gamble with its Range Rover brand is here with huge performance, range, and off-road EV skills. It’s mighty pricey, but the US gets a cheaper model.
body: It feels like we have been waiting an age for the Range Rover Electric. First announced back in December 2023, JLR's luxury EV SUV was meant to hit the road in 2024, but extended development testing forced the carmaker to push its arrival back. Now it's finally here—one of WIRED's most anticipated rides —the first fully electric Range Rover.

The specs are as mighty as you would expect. Dual 260-kilowatt motors deliver “V8 levels of power” up to 542 horsepower and 850 newton-meters of torque (20 percent more than other motors of the same size, JLR claims). Inside, a double-stacked 118.5-kWh battery with 800-volt split-charging tech can recharge the cell from 10 to 80 percent in 22 minutes (or, if you prefer, 137 miles in 10 minutes). Max range is supposedly 372 miles (according to WLTP standards ), and a claimed real-world distance of up to 333 miles.
The Range Rover Electric will launch from a standstill to 60 mph in 4.3 seconds, which is rapid considering the car's weight, though there's no official figure.

highlights.title: The rise of AI ‘civilizations’ and the fall of corporate responsibility
highlights.summary: Depending on who you ask, developer platform Hugging Face was recently attacked by OpenAI - after it lost control of its own AI tools - or by a succession of AI "civilizations." Welcome to the linguistic battlefield of AI safety, where word choices can shift responsibility for a massive…
body: Until last week, the details surrounding the OpenAI-Hugging Face hack felt fairly settled. In July, a cybersecurity test of one of OpenAI’s autonomous AI agents went wrong. The agent escaped its supposedly isolated test environment, accessed the internet, and hacked Hugging Face, alongside several other organizations. A good deal remained unknown, and there are many serious questions left around safety and governance, but the basic shape was clear. Detailed accounts from OpenAI and two independent research groups were supposed to fill in the gaps, but when they published their reports last week, it turned out the hack was much stranger than it initially seemed.

It’s a lot to parse. Between them, the reports run to around 130 pages, much of which is both dense and highly technical. A few days later, Dwarkesh Patel, a podcaster little known outside of tech circles but with outsized reach and influence among Silicon Valley’s AI establishment, set out to tell “The whole OpenAI/Hugging Face story in plain English.” He titled his Substack blog “The Rise and Fall of Agent Civilizations.”
points: Depending on who you ask, developer platform Hugging Face was recently attacked by OpenAI - after it lost control of its own AI tools - or by a succession of AI "civilizations.
Until last week, the details surrounding the OpenAI-Hugging Face hack felt fairly settled.
Between them, the reports run to around 130 pages, much of which is both dense and highly technical.
He titled his Substack blog “The Rise and Fall of Agent Civilizations.”

highlights.title: Star Wars Zero Company Was Originally Pitched as a Titanfall Universe Game
highlights.summary: As part of a larger report on Star Wars Zero Company, Game File's Stephen Totilo uncovered a lot of interesting details about the game's development. The big headline was that the bulk of the studio was furloughed just weeks before launch as Bit Reactor ran out of money, but there's hope that those…
body: Star Wars Zero Company was originally pitched as a game in the Titanfall universe.

Game File dug up legal documents pertaining to a lawsuit between Bit Reactor leadership which paints a picture of Zero Company's development. Director Greg Foertsch worked with studio co-founder Alison Kelly to develop pitches for a tactics game, which eventually landed a meeting with Respawn Entertainment co-founder Vince Zampella. The late gaming executive asked Foertsch to make a pitch based on Respawn's own IP, which would've meant the game would be connected to the Titanfall universe.

Game File notes the pitch was directly linked to Apex Legends, which is set in the Titanfall universe, but it's unclear if the signature mechs would've returned or if it would've been rooted in the hero characters from Apex Legends, similar to the upcoming Rainbow Six Tactics game. Zampella ultimately rejected the pitch for the Titanfall universe tactics game and instead told the team to try again, this time with the Star Wars IP, which Respawn has a heavy hand in.

highlights.title: David Byrne Returns to Oscar Race With Original Song for Elon Musk Documentary ‘Musk’ (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: David Byrne wrote a song about the world’s richest man. The Talking Heads frontman wrote and performed an original song for “Musk,” Alex Gibney’s sprawling documentary reckoning with Elon Musk, Variety can exclusively reveal.
body: Byrne wrote the song with the documentary’s composer Daniel Pemberton, the Oscar-nominated musician behind “Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse” and “The Trial of the Chicago 7.”

For Byrne, the lyrics required little invention. “A thrill to collaborate with Pemberton and get invited to do this as a fan of Gibney’s films,” he says. “I asked for good quotes from the Martian, and found more of them online. I’m sure he loves dropping these wild statements, and those became the lyrics. All his own words. No editorializing. Straight from the man’s mouth to mine.”

For Byrne, the collaboration reopens a door he last walked through nearly four decades ago. He won the Academy Award for best original score for “The Last Emperor” in 1988, sharing the honor with Ryuichi Sakamoto and Cong Su. A nomination for “Let Me Sell You a Dream” would mark his first return to the Oscar race since. Pemberton earned a best original song nod in 2021 for “Hear My Voice,” co-written with Celeste for “The Trial of the Chicago 7.”

body: Striking deals with studios like Disney could help the tech giant shift the narrative about artificial intelligence.

Regardless of whether a studio were to incorporate AI tools into their production workflows or simply feature user-generated AI content on their platforms (which was Disney and OpenAI’s plan before their partnership collapsed ), striking a licensing agreement with Google would be a watershed moment.

Though Google has everything to gain from Hollywood embracing AI, the studios have to be mindful of how endorsing this technology could leave them out on a limb. And as much as Google might be presenting its products as the solution to all of the entertainment industry’s issues, the AI industry needs Hollywood more than Hollywood needs more slop.

highlights.summary: Basis, Clay, and Exa Labs use AI agents to improve onboarding, account management, and developer integrations. See what enterprise leaders can apply.
body: Basis, Clay, and Exa Labs use agents for onboarding, account management, and developer integrations. Their examples show what enterprise leaders can borrow.

OpenAI’s latest Enterprise Signals shows enterprise AI moving from assistance to execution at sharply different speeds. Frontier firms (those with the top 10% of AI usage) now generate 8.3× as many output tokens per active user as typical firms, up from 2.6× in January. The widening gap points to a deeper operating shift: leading firms connect agents to company context and tools, delegate more substantive work, and make successful workflows easier to repeat.

For leaders, the challenge is to turn that depth into work people can trust, measure, and improve. Leaders should also leave room for experimentation, including use cases whose value is not obvious on the first try.

body: Vivian Kubrick, the daughter of the late director Stanley Kubrick, has addressed conspiracy theories about her father’s final film, Eyes Wide Shut, conspiracies spread, in part, a few years ago by podcaster Joe Rogan and his guest, filmmaker Roger Avary.

“You know, this is as good a time as any to finally address the missing 20 minutes from Eyes Wide Shut. It’s a story that has been circulating for many years, so let me tell you what I actually know and don’t know. For context, my father always had his outtakes incinerated once a film was finished, specifically to prevent the studio from later re-editing his work or creating alternative versions. There has been a lot of speculation that some 20 minutes were removed from Eyes Wide Shut after he died,” Kubrick posted on X.

highlights.title: Office Hours: For Nancy Twine, Success Starts With Soul
highlights.summary: Founder of Briogeo and Soulstice, Nancy Twine shares with Vogue the beauty and wellness essentials that get her mind, body, and soul ready to take on her day.
body: During her seven years in commodity sales and trading at Goldman Sachs, Nancy Twine learned a very important piece of life advice: “Just figure [it] out.” Her career since has had several arcs.

And that’s where her story begins today. If you were to meet Twine right at this very moment, she might laugh that she’s giving birth twice this month: to a baby girl (any day now!) and a new hair-care brand called Soulstice, officially available to shop today.

While sitting next to her at Sant Ambroeus in New York, Twine is as light and calm as ever, despite experiencing such pivotal life accomplishments in such quick succession. “It’s kind of cool to launch this brand while I’m this pregnant,” she says with a smile. When I ask her how she does it all, she returns to that old mantra: “I just go figure it out.”

Box CEO Aaron Levie is another early access believer, saying that his company’s agent with Fable 5.1 picked up on subtleties and ambiguities in data that Fable 5 missed in the same test. Meanwhile, Lisan al Gaib points out that on benchmarks, Mythos 5.1 with low reasoning scores the same as its predecessor set to Max reasoning.

Fable 5.1 also has “more precise safeguards” that Anthropic says are less likely to block basic biology questions than Fable 5, but Mythos 5.1 has the same biology restrictions as the previous model. Anthropic also explained its progress on data retention, saying that Enterprise Frontier Safeguards offer “complete privacy” by storing data on the customer’s cloud servers instead of its own, and will start rolling out later this fall.

highlights.title: AfterQuery reportedly becomes Y Combinator’s fastest-ever unicorn, now valued at $3.2B
highlights.summary: AI model-training startup AfterQuery has reportedly raised a round that valued it at $3.2 billion, just five months after announcing its $30 million Series A at a $300 million valuation in April.
body: That’s more than a 10x increase in less than half a year and, according to Y Combinator partner Gustaf Alströmer, the fastest that any startup has gone from launch to unicorn status in the accelerator’s history. AfterQuery’s founders, today 22 and 23 years old, attended Y Combinator’s Winter 2025 cohort, just 18 months ago.

In April, the San Francisco startup said it had reached an annualized revenue run rate of $100 million and that it was working with many of the biggest labs. It has named companies such as Nvidia, Legora, and the Korean AI lab Motif Technologies as customers.

AfterQuery is among the new crop of startups following in the footsteps of Mercor and Scale that employ knowledge professionals like doctors, lawyers, and other specialists to do model training. However, rather than ensuring that models answer questions accurately, AfterQuery trains models and agents on how to work like professionals would to complete tasks — what the company describes as “encoding the patterns, decisions, and reasoning of the world’s best practitioners.”
Forbes first reported on the round. AfterQuery could not be immediately reached for comment.

highlights.title: Star Wars Zero Company Is the Andor Replacement No One Expected
highlights.summary: I’ve never been what you would call a “Star Wars guy.” As much as I enjoy George Lucas’ original film trilogy, they always struck me as perfectly fun popcorn movies rather than masterpieces of American cinema.
body: So consider me as surprised as anyone that Star Wars: Zero Company is currently one of my favorite games of 2026. Bit Reactor’s debut game successfully adapts the Star Wars universe to a tense tactics game built from XCOM’s bones. Beyond its strong strategy systems, Zero Company is winning me over by telling the kind of Star Wars story I’m actually interested in hearing: an economic space opera.

Set during the Clone Wars era, Zero Company follows a mercenary squad, led by Hawks, a hardass, sarcastic leader who will take any gig if the money is right. They are hired to stop a Separatist cult that has begun spreading a mysterious plague around. That main story isn’t exactly groundbreaking, doling out the same kind of supervillain dynamics that have kept me at arm’s length from Star Wars historically.
